member: single actual 1.5-inch solid Douglas Fir-Larch No. 2
bolt: nominal 3/8-inch ASTM A307 Grade A example; delivered grade and thread location unverified
conditions: one steel side member and one wood main member in single shear
full 1.5-inch nominal-diameter wood bearing length and no gap
bolt lateral load only; no bolt-axis tension or prying
full required NDS edge, end, spacing and service conditions assumed, not demonstrated
AISC bolt-shaft value is a separate ASD-style comparator, not a mixed-code joint rating

wood_example_conditions.net_section: one 7/16-inch wood bore through a 1.5 by 5.5-inch member, uniform axial tension parallel to grain, dry reference Ft with no other cuts or adjustments; not a connection rating
wood_example_conditions.washer: one ideal rigid 1-inch outside-diameter washer bearing fully on wood around a 7/16-inch bore, dry Fc-perp and no Cb increase; ignores washer flexure, edge clipping and preload; not extra external-load allowance
wood_example_conditions.row_tear_out: hypothetical two-bolt single row with 3D pitch, at least 7D end distance, force parallel to grain, t=1.5 inches, dry Fv and NDS Appendix E method; not the A66 factory pattern or a multi-bolt rating

interpretation: Under assumed pure-shear conditions, wood bearing Mode Im is a lower reference limit than the A307 bolt-shaft shear comparator. Other wood examples show different action limits and depend on an invented one-hole or minimum two-bolt layout, not on A66 geometry. The actual NDS single-fastener value is the minimum of all applicable yield modes and could be lower. This does not prove wood fracture, establish the A66 angle capacity, cover bolt tension/prying, or validate a multi-bolt joint.
